concerns.text: FR-007 mandates 'multiple-comparison correction (e.g., Bonferroni)' for hypothesis tests across city networks. This requirement has no anchoring User Story. US-1 focuses on threshold identification, US-2 on survival analysis, and US-3 on resource profiling. None of the stories mention cross-city statistical correction or family-wise error rate control. This is an unanchored requirement (scope creep).

FR-009 requires computing 'an independent measure of topological complexity (e.g., betweenness centrality)'. While it cites 'See US-1, Scientific Soundness', US-1's scope is strictly about 'route length' stratification and 'validity percentages'. US-1 does not mention measuring or using topological complexity metrics like betweenness centrality. The requirement introduces a new metric not requested by the anchored story.

FR-008 requires validating the 'local adjacency' graph against an external source (OpenStreetMap). It cites 'See US-1, Scientific Soundness'. However, US-1's scope is limited to evaluating model performance on stratified route lengths. It does not describe a requirement to validate the ground truth graph against an external map source. The 'Scientific Soundness' tag is not a User Story ID, and no story explicitly covers this validation step.

SC-005 requires reporting adjusted p-values from multiple-comparison correction. This success criterion is anchored to FR-007. Since FR-007 itself is unanchored to any User Story (see concern above), SC-005 is also effectively orphaned from the user goals. It measures a metric that no user story requested.

SC-006 requires measuring graph completeness against OpenStreetMap. This is anchored to FR-008. Since FR-008 is not anchored to a User Story (see concern above), SC-006 is orphaned from the user goals. No story describes the need to validate the ground truth graph against an external map.
